physics_goals.quote: MEG: Search for $\mu^+ \to e^+ \gamma$ down to $10^{-13}$ Branching Ratio
physics_goals.value: Search for the charged-lepton-flavor-violating decay μ⁺ → e⁺ γ down to a branching ratio of 10⁻¹³

summary.plain: An experiment at the Paul Scherrer Institute in Switzerland that looked for a muon turning directly into an electron and a burst of light -- a decay the Standard Model forbids. It ran from 2009 to 2013 and did not see the decay, setting a new best limit.
summary.technical: MEG (PSI-R-99-05): searched for μ⁺ → e⁺ γ using a liquid xenon calorimeter and a positron spectrometer (drift chamber + timing counter) on the PSI piE5 DC muon beamline. Data taking 2009-2013, 7.5×10¹⁴ stopped muons on target; superseded by the upgraded MEG II. See result:meg-mu-to-e-gamma-limit-2016 for the final branching-ratio limit.

unique_capabilities.quote: utilize detector elements with best possible resolutions both on the e+ and gamma-sides, so that the background-free identification of the signal down to this small branching ratio can be obtained hopefully with a good margin
unique_capabilities.value: Combined a liquid xenon calorimeter with a positron spectrometer (drift chamber and timing counter) optimized on both the positron and gamma-ray sides for background-free operation at the 10⁻¹³ branching-ratio level, using the world's most intense continuous (DC) muon beam at PSI
